2607.19604.title: Scaling Laws for Hypernetwork-Based Knowledge Injection in Large Language Models
2607.19604.paper_summary: Injecting factual knowledge into large language models (LLMs) reliably and at scale remains an open challenge. Hypernetworks provide a promising solution to large-scale knowledge injection. Although hypernetworks are typically applied for test-time adaptation, we explore their use in train-time knowledge injection, where, given a large corpus of facts, we train a hypernetwork to generate a fixed LoRA adapter that, when inserted into the target model, enable the model to answer questions about those facts. In this work, we investigate whether hypernetworks can be used to perform train-time knowledge injection and how this ability varies with scale. The scaling behavior of hypernetworks remains largely unstudied. Our design decouples the hypernetwork's injection capacity from the target model's general capability, enabling, for the first time, a rigorous study of scaling laws for hypernetwork architectures. We characterize how loss, reasoning accuracy, and out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization vary with hypernetwork depth, width, and target network size. We construct a large-scale dataset, called MegaWikiQA, containing tens of millions of multi-hop question-answer examples across 39 domains constructed from examples in Wikidata5M. Our results reveal: (i) hypernetwork-based injection exhibits broadly predictive power law scaling along all architecture axes; and (ii) hypernetworks are capable of reliable OOD generalization at increasing scales, suggesting that hypernetwork provides a promising alternative to other train-time adaptation methods such as LoRA finetuning and full fine-tuning, exhibiting steeper scaling exponents in all OOD evaluations. Together, these results establish hypernetworks as a principled and scalable substrate for train-time adaptation, and provide the first empirically grounded scaling laws to guide hypernetworks for factual reasoning in large language models.
2607.19604.paper_summary_zh: 將事實知識可靠且大規模地注入大型語言模型（LLMs）仍然是一個未解的挑戰。超網絡為大規模知識注入提供了一個有前景的解決方案。雖然超網絡通常用於測試時適應，但我們探討它們在訓練時知識注入中的應用，這裡，給定一個大型事實語料庫，我們訓練一個超網絡來生成一個固定的LoRA適配器，當其插入目標模型時，能夠使模型回答有關這些事實的問題。在這項工作中，我們研究超網絡是否可以用於執行訓練時知識注入，以及這種能力如何隨著規模而變化。超網絡的擴展行為仍然基本上未被研究。我們的設計將超網絡的注入能力與目標模型的通用能力解耦，首次實現了對超網絡架構擴展法則的嚴謹研究。我們描述了損失、推理準確性和分佈外（OOD）泛化如何隨著超網絡的深度、寬度和目標網絡大小而變化。我們構建了一個大型數據集，稱為MegaWikiQA，包含來自39個領域的數千萬個多跳問題-答案示例，這些示例是從Wikidata5M中的例子構建而來。我們的結果顯示：（i）基於超網絡的注入在所有架構軸上展現出廣泛的預測能力法則擴展；（ii）超網絡能夠在增長的規模下可靠地進行OOD泛化，這表明超網絡為其他訓練時適應方法如LoRA微調和全微調提供了一個有前景的替代方案，在所有OOD評估中展現出更陡的擴展指數。總體而言，這些結果確立了超網絡作為訓練時適應的原則性和可擴展基底，並提供了首個經驗基礎的擴展法則，以指導超網絡在大型語言模型中的事實推理。
